_doc: The AI opponent (src/ai/bot.gd): an economy, a build order, attack waves and counter-picks. Times in seconds; army sizes in population (large units count 2).

economy._doc: max_workers: per age, the most workers it trains. age_workers: with this many it stops training workers and saves for age 2; age3_workers: with this many in age 2 it saves for age 3 (soldiers and research leave the cost alone until the age-up is clicked; the guard trains while it runs). rebalance_every: seconds between moving one gatherer from the resource most over its share to the one most under. Shares: the mix, leaning to what it saves for (the next age: a hundred shares split by what it lacks, the rest halved; a build step waiting on resources: build_push shares); none on a stock of `plenty` (more than it saves for). trade (bot.gd _trade): with a market, gold over `above` buys a lot of the lower of food and wood while it's under `below`; with less gold than `above`, the biggest other pile over `above` is sold; one trade every `every` seconds.

carts._doc: trade carts (bot.gd _trade_carts): from age `age`, every `every` seconds: with two markets far enough apart to trade (ours, or ours and an ally's: the farthest pair), idle carts go on the route and more are trained at our end, one at a time, up to `max`, from what's over beyond what it saves for; second_market 1: with no such pair, a second Town Center far enough from our only market gets a market beside it

_doc_mix: economy.mix: per age, the share of workers on each resource (the bot sends idle and new workers to whatever is furthest below its share, and moves one gatherer at a time over to it)
_doc_build_order: each step: a building, from `age`, once it has `workers`; `near` lays it by the nearest patch of that resource (`away`: at least that many tiles from the Town Center); `builders`: workers sent (2 by default); `count`: how many of that building the step wants in all (default: one more than the steps before it). `save`: a building-up level's soldiers leave its cost alone while it waits (the buildings the ages and the content need, not the extra ones); 2: every level's do (the market: it turns piles nobody spends into the wood and food soldiers need). Steps go in order; a later age's step doesn't hold up this age's. A step it can't afford yet is what it saves for (economy shares). `expand_workers`: the workers it waits for instead on a big map or once home runs thin (expand.town). `own_side`: `near` only by patches nearer us than the enemy (ground we can hold). `guard`: only a level that guards its crossing (levels.guard_crossing) takes this step, once it has been on the back foot (the enemy army it remembers outnumbering its own by land.defend_pct), and lays it on the key crossing (land; where there's no room for it there, by the Town Center). `push`: how hard the economy leans to the step while it waits on resources (economy.build_push by default): the University and the Castle lean harder, so age 3's buildings don't wait on a gentle trickle of wood and stone.

military._doc_waves: waves: set times and the army (population) each needs; then one every repeat_every seconds once the army is repeat_min_army (per age: a Town Center full of workers wants a bigger wave). Soldiers left out in the field under half a wave come home to join the next one.

army_floor._doc: bot.gd _army_floor: once it has `from` workers, no new worker while its soldiers (population) are under pct percent of its workers: dear soldiers (centaurs') get bought instead of a 75-food worker every time

military._doc_most: lines the bot keeps only a few of, out and queued (bot.gd _enough), picked by the counter-pick like any soldier (unlike military.siege.max's engines, which go first): war beasts (D-129), at most 4, and their pick_bias (-30) holds them back until it has seen a crowd of foot soldiers or buildings to break (their bonus against infantry and buildings) and few spears or skirmishers (their bonus against war beasts and large units counts against them)
military._doc_pick_bias: the counter-pick (bot.gd _train: the unit whose attack, hp/10 and bonuses times the foes seen with that class score best, less the bonuses foes have against it) adds this per slot: with nothing seen the Barracks trains spears, as before the swordsman (even the rats, whose swordsman swings a cheese hammer); a few seen spears or skirmishers (the swordsman's bonus) tip it to swords (tests/test_ai.gd pick); the Stable's scouts (-5) only for a few seen healers or skirmishers with no cavalry of ours to hand (the scout for looking is trained apart: scouts), the Range's mounted archers (-6) once three or so foot soldiers are seen and few spears (their bonus against infantry outweighs it), archers otherwise
military._doc_building_foes: while the army goes for an enemy building (bot.gd _aim: a wall shutting the way), the counter-pick counts this many foes of class building, so the line with a bonus against buildings (the swordsman's) is trained for the raid. On (2) since 2026-10-13: with the bots saving better (D-120 prices, the stone and market fix) a palisade ring falls at 17:44 against 18:20 off (the Town Center in reach at 13:30 against 15:55), a stone ring at 19:23 against 19:46, a ring with a gap at 11:52 against 10:47, bot against bot 19:41 against 20:13, and every test_ai piece passes (the stall it caused before, seven swordsmen by 7:00 then none until 13:00, is gone). First tried 2026-10-13 and left off then.
military._doc_hero: the race's hero (Town Center, from age 2; src/sim/heroes.gd, D-159: one a race): trained once the bot has `army` soldiers (`more`: soldiers more for each further one, were a race to have several), saving for it (soldiers leave its price alone while nobody raids us) and training it once it can pay beyond a worker; a fallen one revived the same way as soon as it may; they march with the army (the waves, the defence), and one under `retreat_pct` of its hit points walks home to heal, going back to the fight at `back_pct` (bot.gd _hero)
military._doc_healers: healers (Town Center, from age 2): one per per_army soldiers, up to max per age; kept `behind` tiles back from the army's middle (towards home); idle ones further than `follow` tiles from that spot are sent there every `every` seconds

towers._doc: after a raid on its buildings or workers within `within` tiles of its Town Center (not at the Town Center itself, which shoots), once quiet, it raises a Watchtower by the spot (up to the level's `towers`, one at a time)

shelter._doc: a raid within `tiles` of the Town Center by at least the level's `shelter_pop` of enemy population, more than its soldiers at home can answer: call to arms (workers into the Town Center and towers); back to work once quiet or after `seconds` (the economy stands still inside), and no call again for `every` seconds

military._doc_siege: siege (Siege Workshop and Castle, age 3): the bot keeps at most max of each engine (out and queued; the Castle's sappers and great sling too); on its regroup beats its rams and sappers go for the nearest enemy gate, wall or tower it can see (else any building), its catapults and great slings for a tower within towers_within tiles of them, else they keep with the army
military._doc_walls: walls you stand on (milestone 16, src/ai/walls_ai.gd), every `every` seconds: with walkway walls of its own and no attack out, the bot keeps up to man_pct of its shooters at home up on the wall nearest the nearest enemy it sees (else the side facing the enemy); attacking, its siege tower is pushed to the nearest enemy walkway and, once docked, takes the foot soldiers within climb_tiles of it up and over (down the enemy's stairs at the target). The siege tower is one of military.siege.max
military._doc_raids: A level with `raids` (levels) sends each wave and push at the enemy's economy first: the buildings of raid_targets it remembers (fog memory) that stand out of reach of their shooting buildings (by raid_safe tiles more), in up to `raids` groups of at least raid_min, nearest first; with none left, the Town Center as before.
military._doc_contain: contain_pop, contain_gap: an army smaller than contain_pop (population) doesn't storm a Town Center under the enemy's towers, Castle or Town Center arrows (fog memory): it waits on its way in, contain_gap tiles out of their reach, and goes in once it's that big, or once it brings a siege engine (bot.gd _contain_point). dominant_pct: an army this many percent of the enemy army it remembers (or more) skips raids and goes for the Town Centers (waiting first if it's under contain_pop).
military._doc_press: pressing a lead (bot.lobster press_think, D-198): from `from` seconds, with `workers` workers or more, a bot clearly ahead of the enemy it knows of (an age up, or the same age and workers_pct percent of the enemy's workers as it knows them: those it has seen within scout.memory, or one a building it remembers but walls, if more; ages are announced; and its army at least army_pct percent of the enemy army it remembers) presses home: it masses `army` population (or over_pct percent of the enemy army it remembers, if more; within its level's army_ratio, less a tenth), saving for the soldiers it lacks instead of the next age or a building while it's short of that (at the prices of the soldiers it fields, and its hero if it waits on one; `push`: how hard the economy leans to it, as economy.build_push), its soldiers paying no heed to other savings, and its soldiers at home answering only raids on its own side of the map, not a tower's arrows nor raiders running home, then (or after `wait` seconds of massing, with at least a repeat wave's army) sends all of it, home guard and all, past raids and contain waits at the Town Centers (rams for the Town Center first), reinforces it with every REINFORCE soldiers that gather at home, and calls what's out home to mass again only once its army, reinforcements and all, falls under back_pct percent of the army it massed. It keeps pressing while it holds stay_pct percent of the enemy's workers in no lower age. While pressing, a house goes up once its population is within `headroom` of its cap (2 otherwise), for the soldiers queued everywhere. A level's `press` replaces any of these.
military._doc_scouts: scouts (Stable, from age 2): the bot keeps `keep` units of the scout line, trained ahead of the counter-pick (bot.gd _train_scout); Scout's soldier tours (src/ai/scout.gd) take a scout-line unit before any other soldier, without waiting for an army; more scouts the counter-pick trains fight with the army

research._doc: Besides line upgrades (and gathering, for building-up levels): the economy research it buys (economy, then buildings: the University's, Bastion once it has a tower), and the soldiers' research it buys once that research reaches at least army_min of its soldiers (the armoury track for what it fields). Both keep back what it's saving for (the next age, a blocked build step) once it has the workers to age up.
research._doc_wait_for: wait_for: research it leaves until it has that building (the Bastion's stone waits for the Castle's)

wonder._doc: a Wonder (bot.gd _wonder): from `age`, with none of its own standing or going up, once its stock of every resource is at least spare_pct percent of the Wonder's cost, it lays one by its Town Center and sends `builders` workers. Every bot also attacks a Wonder it knows of (seen, or finished: everyone hears of that) before anything else, and a finished one at once

levels._doc: difficulty, as in the genre: easier bots build up more and fight less, but grow all game (no caps, up to the population limit). delay: seconds added to every wave's time; army_pct: the share of each wave's minimum army; army_ratio: soldiers kept (population) as a percent of its workers per age (50: half its workers in age 1, as many in age 2, one and a half in age 3; absent: no limit); wave_pct: the share of its army each wave sends (the rest defend); build_up: research gathering and line upgrades before soldiers; age3_workers: workers before it saves for age 3 (economy.age3_workers otherwise); towers: Watchtowers it raises where it was raided; shelter_pop: the raid (enemy population) that makes it call its workers to arms (absent: never); all_in: an army this big (population) goes out whole on its wave, home guard and all (absent: never). (Dominic: not caps; less focus on fighting, more building up.) guard_crossing: 1 puts a Watchtower on the key crossing (land). raids: waves and pushes go for the enemy's economy outside tower range first, in up to this many groups (military.raid_targets), from raid_from seconds (Normal: a long match's way out of a stand-off; Hard: from the start). press: changes to military.press (Easy wants a bigger lead and masses less; Hard presses a smaller lead).

scout._doc: src/ai/scout.gd. A worker tours once it has worker_at workers (before worker_before seconds) for up to worker_seconds: round the enemy's start at enemy_tiles, then up to `points` crossings and the middle, nearest next; then back to work. From soldier_age, with an army of soldier_army, the fastest idle soldier at home tours every `every` seconds (soldier_seconds at most). Hit, a scout runs home. Enemy soldiers seen are remembered `memory` seconds (counter-picks read the memory). A unit of the scout line (milestone 13), once there is one, is the soldier that tours, army or not.

land._doc: src/ai/land.gd. One study (a whole-map route search, search_cells cells settled a think: a few thinks each on the big maps) every study_every seconds, each kept fresh: our way (every our_every s), their way (their_every: its crossing is the key crossing), each bridge (bridge_every: a broken one that makes our way to their start mend_pct shorter, or is the only way, is mended by two workers; a standing one whose loss makes their way cut_pct longer is broken by `breakers` melee soldiers once they field cut_enemy population, when we swim or they outnumber us by defend_pct), a detour round enemy fire over our way: archers on a hill, and the towers it remembers that don't stand within target_tiles of the target (each cell under fire costs under_fire more; taken if no more than detour_pct longer), an amphibious flank kept flank_apart cells off our way (no more than flank_pct longer; flank_share percent of a wave of flank_min or more goes that way). guard_tiles, guard_range: a level that guards lays the build order's `guard` Watchtower within guard_tiles of where their way leaves the key crossing on our side, if that's within guard_range tiles of home (if there's room; else where the step says). hills: ranged soldiers with `army` enemy soldiers within `near` tiles step up to higher ground within `tiles` (every `every` s each; looked at every every_check s). road: up to `max` roads, studied every `every` s once there are `workers`: trees at `tree` per cell (open ground 10), the cell beyond `far` tiles (steps across and down) whose way gets shortest, if by `save` tiles and `pct` percent, with no more than `trees` trees, all on our side (distance squared to home under side_pct percent of that to the enemy's start): `fellers` workers fell them, from a lumber camp they lay by it if nothing of ours takes wood within `camp` tiles.

expand._doc: src/ai/expand.gd. camps: per resource the drop-off it builds by far gatherers: with camp_workers or more gathering over camp_tiles from any drop-off of theirs, one goes up by them (camp_builders of them build it; one look every camp_every s). Escorts: a knot of escort_workers gatherers (within post_tiles of each other) beyond guard_tiles from the Town Center gets `escort` soldiers posted (from escort_age, with an army of escort_army; up to `posts` posts; looked at every post_every s; no post within post_tiles of an enemy building it remembers, and an escort that takes on an enemy building rejoins the army). town: the second Town Center's step waits for its expand_workers instead on a map big_map tiles wide or more, or once less than thin.<resource> is left within thin.tiles.
